hci1.title: Introduction to Human-Computer Interaction
hci1.content: What is HCI?Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) refers to the study and design of the interaction between people and computers, focusing on creating user-friendly interfaces. It is a multidisciplinary field involving engineering, psychology, design, and ergonomics.Principles of HCIEffective interface design is guided by core principles:Know Thy User: Consider factors such as age, gender, education level, social status, and technology background.Understand the Task: Ensure the design matches the steps and logic of the user's workflow.Reduce Memory Load: Minimize the amount of information users must memorize to carry out tasks.Strive for Consistency: Use elements consistently across your application so users are not confused.Remind Users: Employ interfaces that give continuous reminders of important information.Prevent Errors: Eliminate error-prone conditions and provide clear notifications or solutions.Naturalness: Favor natural interaction and interfaces close to human-human communication.

hci2.title: Guidelines Categories and Example Guidelines
hci2.content: Characteristics of HCI GuidelinesHCI guidelines are specific, task-based, user-group focused, and platform-dependent rules.Types of GuidelinesUser Type: Tailored for kids, the elderly, or people with disabilities.Platform/System: Designed for mobile, desktop, embedded systems, or public kiosks.Vendor/Brand: Adheres to standards like iOS, Android, Windows, or company branding.Interaction Style: Covers GUI, voice input, gestures, touchscreens, and haptics.General HCI Design GuidelinesVisual Display Layout: Avoid clutter, use alignment and whitespace, and highlight key content.Information Structuring: Organize content logically using navigation aids like breadcrumbs and tabs.Taking User Input: Provide efficient and accurate input methods using drop-downs, checkboxes, and auto-complete.Design for Disabilities: Provide text alternatives for images and allow keyboard-only navigation based on WCAG 2.0.
